defect_headline_line: Thousands of people linked arms around the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts on September 18, forming a human chain in Washington D.C. Crowds gathered in the Foggy Bottom area, carrying signs that read "hands off Kennedy Center" and singing. Actor Lynda Carter addressed the rally. Neal Racioppo, a Washington resident, stated Trump could not get his name on this cherished building, so he was depriving the world of what it could be. Another protester told Agence France-Presse that President Trump did not have a right to decide that an institution, a living memorial to a past president, could be demolished. Chris Raleigh, co-founder of Hands Off the Arts, organized the gathering.
following_body: The demonstration on September 18 followed a week of escalating developments surrounding the 1971 institution. On September 16, an Agence France-Presse photographer captured images of President Trump on Air Force One, looking at a placard labeled "Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED."
